cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the believers in Galatia, and he's just told them each one is a son now, and an heir through God. But friend, this next part gets PERSONAL. He takes them back to the days before they knew God.

cards.question: Before they knew God, the Galatians were ___ to those who by nature are not gods.

cards.text: But now they know God, or rather, Paul says, they are known by God. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer where nobody even knew I was there, so trust me, being known is a BIG deal.

cards.question: Now that the Galatians know God, what does Paul say they're doing?

answers.text: Going back to weak and worthless principles
Chasing after rich and powerful friends
Arguing over small and petty disputes

cards.question: Paul asks the Galatians if they want to be enslaved by those weak and worthless principles all over again.

cards.text: Then Paul stops talking in general and names something the Galatians are actually doing. He's not guessing, friend. He's got receipts.

cards.question: What does Paul say the Galatians are observing?

answers.text: Special days and months and seasons and years
Strict fasts and vows and washings and prayers
Holy foods and drinks and robes and oils

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians he fears for them. What is he afraid of?

answers.text: That his efforts for them were in vain
That they will never write back to him
That they will run him out of town

cards.text: Then Paul pleads with them: "I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you."

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians they have done him wrong.

cards.text: Then Paul takes them back to the first time he preached the gospel to them. Spoiler, friend: it was NOT his best day.

cards.question: Paul reminds the Galatians why he first preached the gospel to them. What was the reason?

cards.text: Paul's illness was a trial to them. Most folks see a sick guest coming up the walk and suddenly remember they left the oven on, but the Galatians didn't despise him or reject him.

cards.question: Paul was sick when he came, but the Galatians didn't reject him. How did they welcome him?

answers.text: As if he were an angel of God
As if he were a king of Israel
As if he were a long lost brother

cards.question: Paul says the Galatians welcomed him as if he were Christ Jesus Himself.

cards.text: Paul is still thinking about how the Galatians first welcomed him, and now he asks them, "What then has become of your blessing?" He remembers what they would have handed over for him back then.

cards.question: What does Paul say the Galatians would have given him back then?

cards.text: Their own EYES, friend, and I know folks who won't even give up their parking spot for me! Then Paul asks the Galatians a hard question.

cards.question: Paul asks if he has now become the Galatians' ___ by telling them the truth.

cards.text: Then Paul talks about some other people. He says those people are zealous for the Galatians, but not in a good way.

cards.question: Paul says those people aren't zealous for the Galatians in a good way. What does he say they want to do to the Galatians?

answers.text: Isolate them from Paul and those with him
Take their money and their homes from them
Hand them over to the local rulers

cards.question: Paul says those people want the Galatians to be zealous for them.

cards.text: You know the type: the coworker who's suddenly your BEST friend, but only if you leave your old group chat and join theirs. Then Paul has something to say about being zealous itself.

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians that being zealous is never a good thing.
Paul says it's good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose. When does he say that should happen?

answers.text: At any time and not just when he's with them
Only when he is there with them in person
Only when they meet together to pray

cards.text: Then Paul calls the Galatians his children. And he says he's going through something for them all over again.

cards.question: Paul calls the Galatians his children. What pains does he say he's in for them again?

answers.text: The pains of a long fast

cards.question: How long does Paul say he'll be in those pains for the Galatians?

answers.text: Until Christ is formed in them
Until he sees them face to face
Until they send word back to him

cards.text: AGAIN, friend! I get grumpy when my oven timer goes off twice, and Paul is signing up for round two of THIS.

cards.question: Paul says he wishes he could be with the Galatians right now. What would he change?

cards.text: Why? Because, he says, he's perplexed about them. But he still calls them his children, and I bet he hasn't stopped hoping.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin was in the junk drawer "where nobody even knew I was there." His backstory says the opposite. The Millers slid him into the drawer, and his drawer friends knew him well: he welcomed every newcomer, and they held their breath together whenever the drawer opened. The line changes his own story. Something like "where everybody forgot I was there" fits the backstory and keeps the joke.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the exact list in 4:10 ("special days and months and seasons and years"). The setup card only says Paul names something the Galatians are doing, so nothing points to the right answer over the made-up lists. This is guessing the wording of the letter, like the bad Psalm 23 "anoint" example. A question about meaning would work better, such as why Paul brings these observances up after asking about going back to weak and worthless principles.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says. Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: "Those people" first appear here, introduced only as "some other people." The baker isn't told who they are. Earlier in the letter, Paul describes them as some who are troubling the Galatians and trying to distort the gospel of Christ (Galatians 1:7). That can be said simply, with its reference.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to 4:19, which cards 11 to 13 already covered. It doesn't move the baker forward, so it works as a recap card. It also says Paul is "signing up" for the pains again. The text doesn't say Paul chose this, so the joke adds something to Paul's situation. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage along, such as the setup for 4:20.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 6 of the 9 choice cards in stop 2 (cards 2, 6, 10, 12, 13 and 15). True or false has 2 and fill in the blank has 1. Cards 12, 13 and 15 are also three multiple choice cards almost in a row. Stop 1 leans the same way, with 5 of its 9 choice cards multiple choice.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
